event.summary: Check whether removing inherited grid size leaves any attachment path using an obsolete size
event.detail: Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e. TLDR: a surviving caller that expects the grid to preserve its prior size could attach or resize the program at dimensions different from the pane. Details: the assigned patch removes options.size from fitted initialization and the first-fit early return; grid-terminal.js now starts fitted at DEFAULT_SIZE and computes the first observation normally. SPEC_impl.md:1835-1855 says terminal.js mounts the grid before the socket exists because the URL carries its fitted size, and no sizing state is retained across visits. Suggested bucket: high/material UX if a surviving dependency is established; could-be-highest: no established security or loss-of-work route. Confidence: unverified, caller investigation pending. proposed_drop: false. possible_cover: none. Checks made: complete assigned patch read and pinned grid-client contract read; these establish the changed behavior but not all callers. Missing premise: whether any shipped construction or reconnect path still supplies or depends on inherited options.size. Next source check: enumerate pinned farhelmGridTerminal.create callers, inspect first fit and socket URL construction. No execution or reproduction performed.

event.summary: Inherited-size removal has no surviving production dependency
event.detail: Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e. TLDR: considered whether removing inherited sizing could attach or resize the program at dimensions different from the pane; source checks refute a surviving dependency. Details: grid-terminal.js:407 initializes DEFAULT_SIZE and :474-497 computes its normal first fit; a pinned git grep of UI src/assets finds exactly one production farhelmGridTerminal.create call, terminal.js:4313. Its complete options object at :4313-4365 supplies no size. terminal.js:3389-3393 installs the component, fits it and reads grid.size before constructing the socket URL at :3424-3426. sendResize at :4560-4565 reads the grid's fitted size; :4596-4605 sends it again on socket open, covering resize during handshake. Therefore the removed renderer-swap exception has no surviving caller that requires its inherited answer. SPEC_impl.md:1842-1852 says "mounts the grid component for every terminal before the socket exists, because the socket URL carries its fitted size" and "no per-terminal sizing state is retained across visits"; source implements that contract. Suggested bucket if the disproved route existed: high/material UX. Could-be-highest: no, no established security or loss-of-work route. Confidence: confirmed source refutation. proposed_drop: no surviving options.size caller; ordinary first-fit size is read before attach and sent again on open. possible_cover: none. No tests, builds or reproductions run. Scope caveat: this conclusion concerns the removed inherited-size exception, not a general proof of every fitting edge case.

event.summary: Inherited-size removal has no surviving production dependency
event.detail: Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e. TLDR: considered whether removing inherited renderer sizing could attach or resize the terminal program at dimensions different from the pane. The specific surviving-caller route is refuted by source, including reconnect and handshake ordering; this does not certify every size or pixel-timing edge case. Details: grid-terminal.js:407 starts fitted at DEFAULT_SIZE and :474-497 computes the ordinary first fit. The sole production farhelmGridTerminal.create caller is terminal.js:4313; its full options object at :4313-4365 supplies no size. terminal.js:3389-3393 assigns the new component before calling fit, then reads grid.size before constructing the URL at :3424-3426. The component constructor itself finishes by measureChar/currentCell/watchPixelRatio at grid-terminal.js:1961-1963, with no synchronous fit callback before the component is assigned. fit updates fitted before invoking onResize (:495-497); sendResize reads grid.size rather than callback arguments (:4560-4565). A fit during CONNECTING retains its answer while sendResize declines the not-yet-open socket; onopen sends the latest answer at :4594-4605. Later window and pane observations invoke that mount's grid.fit (:4606-4636), and a hello mismatch also requests its fitted size (grid-terminal.js:1984-1988). Reconnect creates a fresh component: terminal.js:1556-1579 saves only the old component as a snapshot, unmounts it, then invokes mountWhenReady. Unmount removes the old window listener and pane observer (:4769-4774), nulls all old socket callbacks before close (:4810-4814), freezes a retained grid and removes its island entry (:4819-4831). freeze irreversibly clears send and onResize (grid-terminal.js:2075-2084); restoration installs the held component only as a non-live tombstone (terminal.js:1614-1629). Thus neither a retained snapshot nor a replacement attachment needs inherited options.size, and the old snapshot cannot send a resize into the replacement. The global font-size operation targets islands, excluding the held/tombstone component (terminal.js:2715-2717). Contract: SPEC_impl.md:1842-1852 says "mounts the grid component for every terminal before the socket exists, because the socket URL carries its fitted size" and "no per-terminal sizing state is retained across visits". Its terminal-size contract says a held reconnect/takeover screen is frozen with no program to tell; the checked lifecycle implements that boundary. Suggested bucket if the refuted route existed: high/material UX. Could-be-highest: no established security or loss-of-work route. Confidence: confirmed source refutation for inherited-size dependency. proposed_drop: no surviving options.size caller; new components own fitted dimensions, handshake open resends them, and retained components lose their resize sink. possible_cover: none; no coverage sources consulted. Synthesis revision adds lifecycle and ordering evidence and preserves the original potential consequence and narrow scope. Interface to g084/g085 onward: grid owns fitted dimensions and commits them before callbacks; terminal.js owns socket availability, URL sizing, open-time resend, observer lifetime and replacement construction. No claim that a browser has measured every layout/pixel change before onopen, or that unrelated timing behavior is correct. No tests, builds or reproductions run; all conclusions are source-supported.
